text:
mika: Quick recap from today's dedicated GPU orchestration sync. Idea: "burst vouchers" + a short "stabilize window" to avoid scale oscillation when tenants spike. High level + config sketch below.

toby: can you give a one-paragraph lifecycle?

mika: tenant requests a voucher to burst. If headroom and voucher available, admit into burst lane and emit a scale intent. The controller opens a stabilize window (base 60s) during which nodes for that intent are protected from immediate delete/eviction. Vouchers are debited on admission; repeated bursts increase voucher cost via a decay/penalty multiplier. If demand falls while window active we drain pods but keep nodes until window end. If provisioning fails fallback to model-variant routing, cross-region when allowed, or queue with TTL and refund.

rina: how to prevent cluster-level overcommit when many tenants burst?

mika: global governor: max_burst_headroom_pct (default 12%). If cumulative headroom >= governor, new admits are rejected with 429 and suggested backoff. Governor adjusts down as cluster utilization rises (e.g., governor = max(4, 18 - util_p95/6)).

sam: what metrics and operator knobs?

mika: metrics: voucher_balance{tenant}, burst_admits, stabilize_window_sec, consecutive_burst_count{tenant}, scale_pending_seconds, p95_provision_latency. Knobs: base_window_sec, adaptive_multiplier_p95, micro_voucher_daily, long_voucher_weekly, penalty_alpha, global_burst_headroom_pct. We expose policy presets: conservative, balanced, aggressive.

toby: rollout plan?

mika: sim harness replaying 30 days of traces in staging (2w), staging canary (1w), pilot on two low-risk tenants (3w), feature flag rollback gates with metric thresholds. I'll open an RFC follow-up with the config and cost delta model.

ops-bot: RFC link updated -> https://redwood.rfc/internal/burst-voucher-proto

rina: +1, also please add support playbook for TTL refunds and an observability doc for sales.

mika: will do, opening PR today.
